subject: Implausibly high random effect from iCAR logistic regression

messages.author: 4a4cf4f06dc9f69d
messages.subject: Implausibly high random effect from iCAR logistic regression
parts:
Dear all, 

I am fitting a relatively simple logistic regression with an iCAR (3,033 observations, with 6.5% 1's). But this model returns implausibly high and skewed random effect variance estimates. I would be very grateful for advice on diagnosing the root cause of this?



Reprex (data available on request, as I can't seem to post it here)

library(INLA)
library(spdep)
reprex_df_1 <- readRDS(file = "reprex_df_1.rda")

###  Define neighbours ###
naighbour_matrix  <- poly2nb(reprex_df_1)
nb2INLA("Analysis.graph", naighbour_matrix)
Analysis.adj <- paste(getwd(), "Analysis.graph", sep ="/")
Analysis.Inla.nb <- inla.read.graph(filename = "Analysis.graph")

### Fit a model with one fixed effect and the iCAR ###
formula_1 <- PACTO_01 ~ T_sp_km2_level + f(ID,  model = "besag",  graph = Analysis.Inla.nb,  adjust.for.con.comp=TRUE, scale.model=TRUE,   constr = TRUE)
Model_1 <- inla(formula_1, family = "binomial",  data = reprex_df_1,  control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE))

prec <- Model_1$summary.hyperpar
var <- 1/prec

Many thanks

Please try this Dropbox transfer (sorry, it's too large to attach): https://www.dropbox.com/t/kHM52Ni9fDtZppBn

Additionally, here is the code I used to create the figure in the opening question. 

### Approach suggested by Blangiardo and Cameletti to get the odds.
library(ggplot2)

# How many areas?
Nareas <- nrow(Model_1$summary.random$ID)

# Extract the marginal posterior distribution for each element of the random effect
csi <- Model_1$marginals.random$ID[1:Nareas]

# Apply the exponential transformation and calculate the posterior mean for each of
# them using the lapply function.
zeta <- lapply(csi, function(x) inla.emarginal(exp,x))

# Add to DF
zeta_DF <- do.call("rbind", zeta)
reprex_df_1$zeta <- zeta_DF

# Plot
p2 <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = reprex_df_1, aes(fill = zeta), colour=NA) +
  guides(fill=guide_legend(title="Posterior mean for\nthe random effects (odds)")) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low='#a50026', mid="#ffffbf", high='#006837')

p2
